story_text.value:
Built a codex like harness for non-tech builders to easily clone B2B SaaS using open-weight models.

We figured companies are still charging for building software. Software, we think is commoditized. Tokens are cheap, and intelligence is open. What's the point of billing tokens.

We want to take the power back from big labs and democratize the power of SoTA LLMs for every builder out there. 1M output tokens shouldn't cost 10s of dollars.

Lots of work to be done but we built a harness that can use open weight models from open router to build SaaS clones.

Give it a shot and lmk what you guys think. We are giving away a generous free tier of open weight model credits along with a lot of SaaS templates that you can start with.

title.value: Show HN: Harness for building/cloning SaaS using open-weight models

We made Backplane to actually use Fable, Astra, etc. as real electrical engineers! It incorporates KiCad + your favorite harness (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Grok) to accelerate hardware development. You can use it "autonomously" or work alongside the agent, making changes or comments to redirect the agent as it works. Also has some slick skills for schematic editing, BOM management.

Hardware is in its "tab to accept changes"/copilot era rather than its agentic era imo.

story_text.value:
Hi all - we just relaunched https://millionshort.com. It's a search engine - rebuilt from the ground up.

Core idea is still around control: Block (or boost) the top 100, 1k, 10k or 1M most popular sites from your results and see what's underneath.

- Ad free / private - Boost/block sites - We run a classifier on all sites so you can filter by things like Topics: Art, Business, Education etc. and formats like Comments, Blogs etc. (Boost/block based on these) - Bringing in some data points like DNS traffic etc. - Handy shopping results that - small/Web - lots of independent/personal sites/blogs - Realtime search (bluesky etc.) - I think largest index of Discord server/content

Would love any feedback - many thanks.

story_text.value:
It's a new feature I've added to Pour Decision.

The idea is:

1. Set an interval on your phone and slip it in your pocket

2. The phone vibrates in your pocket on every interval

3. Condition yourself to have sips when you feel the vibration

Benefits:

- You end up drinking way less in a night than you normally would

- You don't feel like you're moderating cus you're never without a drink

- It's discreet so people you're drinking with won't know you're doing this

This is sort of like a HIIT-timer, but to preserve battery I took another approach. It works by pre-scheduling on-device notifications when you start the timer. iOS allows apps to schedule up to 64 notifications. If you were to set say 5-minute intervals, that covers the next 320 minutes - more than 5 hours. The phone uses no battery in between intervals, and only wakes up the device once every 5 minutes, so battery drain is negligible.

Here's a write-up about it if interested:

https://pourdecision.app/blog/sip-pacing-method

Nine is chock full of features, with FaceTime and couch multiplayer, Apple Watch companion app with live sync, and rotor based accessibility supports as some of the hardest to find in the marketplace.

Above all, I hope that this app finds people who are seeking calm sudoku gaming with or against friends who are long distances away or gathering for the holidays around the TV.
